mws.ponder.tag.data_center.description: Servers, and everything it takes to keep them running
mws.ponder.server_rack_basics.text_1: Server Racks are 240 V machines, powered from a Create: Power Grid network
mws.ponder.server_rack_basics.text_2: Wire the supply into Feed A: the red and blue inlets on the back
mws.ponder.server_rack_basics.text_3: Right-click with Server Blades to fill it, up to four per rack
mws.ponder.server_rack_basics.text_4: With power within 5%% of 240 V, the rack boots and comes online
mws.ponder.server_rack_basics.text_5: If the voltage drifts more than 15%% while it runs, the server crashes and may lose data
mws.ponder.server_rack_basics.text_6: Once the power is clean again, it reboots by itself
mws.ponder.server_rack_basics.text_7: Every watt a server draws turns into heat. One blade cools itself, two run throttled, and more need a Chiller
mws.ponder.server_rack_basics.text_8: Engineer's Goggles show a rack's temperature, its power, and why it won't boot
mws.ponder.server_rack_basics.text_9: Sneak and right-click with an empty hand to pull a blade back out
mws.ponder.server_rack_cabinet.text_1: Stack racks into a cabinet. The whole stack runs from the inlets on the bottom rack
mws.ponder.server_rack_cabinet.text_2: The base has two inlets. Feed A is red and blue, Feed B is orange and cyan
mws.ponder.server_rack_cabinet.text_3: The cabinet splits its load between both feeds
mws.ponder.server_rack_cabinet.text_4: If one feed fails, the other carries the whole cabinet and every server stays online
mws.ponder.server_rack_cabinet.text_5: A single feed works too. Two separate supplies, or a UPS on one of them, keep the cabinet up through outages
mws.ponder.server_rack_cabinet.text_6: The cabinet keeps its stored data in the base rack, and computers can reach it through any rack
mws.ponder.ups.text_1: A UPS sits between the mains and your servers
mws.ponder.ups.text_2: Mains goes into the input on the left of its back panel...
mws.ponder.ups.text_3: ...and the servers plug into the output on the right
mws.ponder.ups.text_4: While the mains is healthy, the UPS passes it through and charges its battery
mws.ponder.ups.text_5: When the mains fails, it switches to battery instantly. The servers never notice
mws.ponder.ups.text_6: A comparator reads its charge. Right-click with an empty hand to switch the output on or off
mws.ponder.chiller.text_1: A full rack makes far more heat than it can shed on its own
mws.ponder.chiller.text_2: A Chiller pulls heat out of every rack within 6 blocks. It runs on 240 V too
mws.ponder.chiller.text_3: It evaporates water to do it, so pipe water in from any side
mws.ponder.chiller.text_4: Once a rack runs warmer than 30 °C, the chiller starts working
mws.ponder.chiller.text_5: Some of that water comes back as sludge. Pipe it away, or the chiller dumps it on the floor
mws.ponder.water_intake.text_1: The Water Intake pulls water out of whatever lake, river or moat it touches
mws.ponder.water_intake.text_2: When powered, it takes the nearest source block every second, reaching up to 16 blocks through connected water
mws.ponder.water_intake.text_3: Pump water out of it with Create pipes and send it on to a Chiller
